summary.name: Introduction to Cloud Native Computing
summary.one_liner: A long-form overview article explaining cloud native computing, its architecture principles (containers, microservices, Kubernetes), development practices, and the role of the Cloud Native Computing Foundation.
use_cases: learning what cloud native computing means
choosing tools for containers and monitoring
planning a move from monolith to microservices
summary.what_it_does: The article defines cloud native computing as building and managing services with containers, microservices, immutable infrastructure and declarative APIs, and contrasts it with monolithic client-server systems. It outlines key characteristics (microservices, containerization, dynamic orchestration, scalability, resilience) and compares cloud native applications with traditional ones on architecture, deployment, and scaling. It lists common development tools such as Docker, Kubernetes, git, Jenkins, Terraform and Prometheus, and describes CI/CD, DevOps integration, and microservices migration steps. It also covers the CNCF and sample projects like Kubernetes, containerd, Prometheus, Envoy and Fluentd, plus security and monitoring considerations.
notable: Covers the CNCF and its major open source projects such as Kubernetes, containerd, Prometheus, Envoy and Fluentd
Explains the shift from monolithic architectures to microservices and containers
Includes sections on cloud native security (DevSecOps, IAM, service meshes) and monitoring tools
caveats: Article is a general overview and does not describe a single product or tool
Page text is cut off in the monitoring section, so later tools (such as New Relic) are not covered
